hot_topics.topic: TP-Link plans US router manufacturing to bypass ban
hot_topics.synthesis: TP-Link announced plans to invest nearly $1 billion in assembling Wi-Fi routers in the United States, aiming to start by 2027. This strategic move is intended to appease the Trump administration and secure approval to sell its new Wi-Fi 8 product line to American consumers. The initiative promises to create hundreds of high-paying jobs in the US.

hot_topics.topic: Google integrates Gemini AI's personal intelligence into cars
hot_topics.synthesis: Google is expanding its Gemini AI assistant's Personal Intelligence feature to automotive platforms, including Android Auto and Apple CarPlay, as well as Google Built-in vehicles. This allows the AI to access personal data from services like Gmail and Calendar to deliver more contextually aware and personalized responses to drivers. The optional feature aims to enhance hands-free assistance and navigation capabilities.

hot_topics.topic: Critical PHP security vulnerabilities prompt emergency patches
hot_topics.synthesis: PHP maintainers are releasing emergency patches for two severe vulnerabilities, both rated 9.2 out of 10 for severity, including a critical Remote Code Execution (RCE) flaw dubbed 'PHP2Shell' discovered with AI. Website administrators are strongly advised to prepare for immediate upgrades, as the patches are expected imminently to address these significant security risks.

hot_topics.topic: GM accelerates AI and software integration for future vehicles
hot_topics.synthesis: General Motors is transforming into a software-defined technology company, unveiling ambitious AI and autonomous vehicle initiatives at its 'Onward' event. The company aims to halve vehicle development times and integrate significantly more powerful compute units, along with giving its OnStar connected car service an AI-powered overhaul. This strategy seeks to enhance vehicle intelligence and user experience.

hot_topics.topic: Documentary 'You Can See Everything' sparks debate on Elizabeth Holmes' psychology
hot_topics.synthesis: Nathan Fielder's new documentary, 'You Can See Everything,' delves into the psychological aspects of Elizabeth Holmes, portraying her as a master of deception and manipulation. The film has prompted discussions, including one economist's argument that Holmes, despite her fraud conviction, should not be in prison due to having young children and the non-violent nature of her crimes, advocating for restitution instead.

hot_topics.topic: US and Russia explore diplomatic paths amid Ukraine conflict
hot_topics.synthesis: Russia has indicated its readiness to resume peace talks with Ukraine and the United States, following a meeting between President Vladimir Putin and US envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg. This diplomatic engagement also saw Russia release imprisoned US citizen Stephen Hubbard at President Trump's request. Despite these developments, tensions remain, with leaders like Trump and Zelensky still at odds over US policy towards Ukraine.

items.title: When it started to burn
items.summary: This video essay explores the profound human impact of four years of war through the eyes of Ukrainian civilians, depicting their experiences of horrific violence, enduring terror, and unwavering solidarity. It offers a poignant perspective on the conflict's toll.

items.title: Does opting out of smart TV tracking work? Research finds “suspicious” traffic.
items.summary: Research reveals that smart TVs from major brands like Samsung, Vizio, and Roku continue to send user data to tracking endpoints despite users opting out, posing significant privacy concerns. This data, collected by Automatic Content Recognition (ACR), is used for viewership measurement and targeted advertising.

items.title: Gemini's Personal Intelligence is coming to cars
items.summary: Google is rolling out Gemini's Personal Intelligence feature to Android Auto and vehicles with Google Built-in, enabling the AI to leverage user data from apps like Gmail and Calendar for more personalized responses. This optional feature, previously paid, will enhance the AI's contextual understanding within cars.

items.title: JustWatch, which tackles streaming fragmentation, launches own streaming service
items.summary: JustWatch, known for guiding users through streaming options, has launched its own ad-supported streaming service, JustWatch TV. The new platform offers a selection of free movies, some unavailable elsewhere, along with rental options.

items.title: Meta drops the word "train" from its commercial TOS after AI backlash
items.summary: Meta removed the word "train" from its commercial terms of service following criticism that the language implied permission to scrape websites linked on business pages for AI training data. The change aims to address concerns raised by legal experts about potential intellectual property issues and licensing fee avoidance.

items.title: PHP warns it plans to release 2 emergency patches imminently
items.summary: PHP maintainers announced impending emergency patches for two critical vulnerabilities, rated 9.2 out of 10 in severity, urging website administrators to prepare for immediate upgrades. The patches are expected within 12 hours, with potential earlier release if details become public or exploitation is detected.

items.title: TP-Link tries to appease Trump admin with pledge to assemble routers in US
items.summary: TP-Link announced plans to begin assembling Wi-Fi routers in the US by 2027, an effort to gain approval from the Trump administration to sell its newest Wi-Fi 8 product line to American consumers. The company signed a Letter of Intent with Keytronic for domestic manufacturing in Mississippi.

items.title: Ukraine’s drone rescue of wounded soldier puts much touted idea into practice
items.summary: Ukraine successfully used a heavy hexacopter drone to evacuate a wounded soldier from a dangerous frontline, marking an unprecedented and historic application of drone technology for casualty rescue. This event demonstrates practical battlefield innovation, moving beyond previous military experimentation with similar concepts.

items.title: 'Trash Island' or DC landmark? How a golf course got Trump in a messy legal dispute
items.summary: President Trump is involved in a legal dispute over his plans to convert a 106-year-old public golf course in Washington D.C. into a tournament-capable venue for professionals. Local golfers have expressed dissatisfaction with the proposed changes to the "Trash Island" course.

items.title: Alberta's decisive decision to stay in Canada gives Carney backing to take on Trump
items.summary: Alberta's overwhelming decision to remain part of Canada has provided Mark Carney with political leverage to challenge Donald Trump's economic policies and focus on restructuring Canada's economy. This vote strengthens Carney's position for national economic leadership.

items.title: Australian MP loses both legs after alleged car attack, husband says
items.summary: An Australian Member of Parliament reportedly lost both legs following an alleged car attack, with the 43-year-old accused attacker, Brendan Nugent, facing multiple charges. This severe incident has led to legal proceedings.

items.title: BBC inside Australian court as man charged with attacking MP stays silent in first hearing
items.summary: During his initial court appearance in Wangaratta, Brendan Nugent, the 43-year-old man charged with attacking Australian MP Helen Haines, remained silent. The BBC reported from inside the courtroom as details of the alleged assault were presented.

items.title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze
items.summary: A "Super El Niño" weather phenomenon has intensified months-long fires in Borneo, Indonesia, leading to widespread toxic haze and causing illness among hundreds of thousands of people. The fires highlight the severe environmental and health impacts of climate-related events.

items.title: Cornell Jane Doe says embattled university head doubted her gang-rape allegation
items.summary: A "Jane Doe" at Cornell University alleges that the institution's embattled head doubted her gang-rape accusation, a claim the university describes as "incorrect." This controversy unfolds as a no-confidence vote against the university leadership looms.

items.title: Family of prison officer killed by IRA receives state apology
items.summary: The family of Brian Stack, a prison officer killed by the IRA in 1983, has received a state apology for his death. Stack was shot in Dublin and died 18 months later from his injuries.

items.title: Gambia to pay victims of Yahya Jammeh's rule from proceeds of his seized US mansion
items.summary: The Gambia confirmed it will compensate victims of former ruler Yahya Jammeh's regime using $2.5 million received from the sale of his seized mansion in Maryland, USA. This initiative aims to provide restitution to those affected by his rule.

items.title: Haitian migrants changed this US town - Trump's deportation drive is reshaping it again
items.summary: Springfield, Ohio, a town previously transformed by Haitian migrants, is now being reshaped by President Trump's deportation policies, placing it at the center of the ongoing immigration debate. The article revisits a false "pet-eating" claim by Trump that drew attention to the town.

items.title: Huge crowds watch attempt to rescue shark stranded in South Korean canal
items.summary: Large crowds gathered to witness a third attempt to rescue a 9-foot-10-inch shark that became stranded in a South Korean canal. Efforts are underway to guide the large marine animal back to the open sea.

items.title: Is Ebola under control in Kenya after nine cases confirmed?
items.summary: The US has issued an advisory for its citizens to reconsider travel to Kenya after nine Ebola cases were confirmed, although the Kenyan government is attempting to reassure the public that the situation is under control. This creates concern despite official reassurances.

items.title: Katya Adler: France divided over who to blame for riots and what to learn from them
items.summary: Both within France and internationally, there is significant disagreement regarding the causes of recent widespread urban unrest and the appropriate lessons to be drawn from it. This division highlights the complex social and political factors at play.

items.title: Macron accuses foreign leaders of exploiting French riots
items.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron accused unnamed foreign leaders, in an apparent reference to Benjamin Netanyahu and Donald Trump, of exploiting the recent French riots. Macron's comments suggest concerns about external political interference amidst domestic unrest.

items.title: Nigeria confirms Ebola case linked to East Africa
items.summary: Nigeria has confirmed an Ebola case linked to East Africa, involving a non-Nigerian female patient who is currently isolated in an Abuja hospital. Health authorities are working to contain the spread of the virus.

items.title: Pakistan arrests man wanted by US over $126m postage fraud case
items.summary: Pakistan has arrested Faheem Akram, a man wanted by the US in connection with a $126 million postage fraud case, who allegedly sold over 5 million fake postage labels. This apprehension marks a significant development in an international fraud investigation.

items.title: Russia says it is ready to resume talks with Ukraine and US to end war
items.summary: Russia has declared its readiness to resume peace talks with Ukraine and the US, following a meeting between President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump's special envoy, Steve Witkoff, in St Petersburg. This signals a potential diplomatic opening to end the ongoing conflict.

items.title: Trump and Zelensky at loggerheads despite new optimism
items.summary: Despite new optimism surrounding potential US-Ukraine policy shifts, President Trump and Ukrainian leader Zelensky remain at odds, fueling misgivings about the future of US support for Ukraine. The dynamics between the two leaders continue to be complex and uncertain.

items.title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge
items.summary: President Trump is facing a lawsuit over the imposition of tariffs on Canada, with plaintiffs arguing that the White House exceeded its authority and caused immediate harm to American businesses. This legal challenge disputes the legality and economic impact of the tariffs.

items.title: Compromised LiteLLM 1.107.0 on PyPI Installs a Credential Stealer and Backdoor
items.summary: A compromised version of LiteLLM 1.107.0 distributed on PyPI has been found to install a credential stealer and a backdoor. Users are warned about the severe security vulnerability in this release.

items.title: DuckDB 2.0.0 LTS “Cinnamon Teal”
items.summary: DuckDB announced the release of its 2.0.0 LTS version, code-named "Cinnamon Teal." This update likely includes significant improvements and long-term support for the in-process SQL OLAP database management system.

items.title: Eight Bits of Trust; eMudhra's CA keys cracked in milliseconds
items.summary: Reports indicate that eMudhra's Certificate Authority (CA) keys were compromised and cracked in milliseconds, exposing a severe security vulnerability. This incident, titled "Eight Bits of Trust," highlights critical issues in digital trust infrastructure.

items.title: Patch the Planet: global response coordination as agents uncover vulnerabilities
items.summary: This item links to "Patch the Planet," an initiative focused on global response coordination, where AI agents collaborate to uncover software vulnerabilities. The project aims to improve cybersecurity through collective discovery and patching efforts.

items.title: PHP 8.2.35
items.summary: PHP has released version 8.2.35, which likely includes various bug fixes and security updates. This is a routine maintenance release for the widely used scripting language.

items.title: PHP2Shell: AI uncovers critical RCE in PHP
items.summary: A critical Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability in PHP, dubbed "PHP2Shell," has been discovered with the aid of AI. This vulnerability poses a significant security risk to web applications using PHP.

items.title: Whatever Happened to Fire Escapes
items.summary: This article explores the historical evolution and decline of fire escapes, questioning their eventual disappearance from modern building codes and construction practices. It delves into the reasons behind this shift and the alternative safety measures now in place.

items.title: Here’s the tea
items.summary: An MIT historian discovered that a Chinese tea chest label, long believed to be from the 1773 Boston Tea Party, actually dates to the 1860s or 1870s. This finding, based on Cantonese text analysis, reveals how ordinary objects acquire historical authority and how collective memory is constructed.

items.title: Interspecies communication
items.summary: Researchers are leveraging advanced AI and devices like hydrophones to decode complex animal communication, aiming to understand different species' inner lives and potentially enable two-way communication. Projects like the Earth Species Project are training large language models on animal sounds to detect patterns and interpret vocalizations.

items.title: “You Can See Everything” and the nature of liars
items.summary: Nathan Fielder's documentary "You Can See Everything" explores the psychology of Elizabeth Holmes, portraying her as a master of deception and manipulation rather than focusing solely on her proven fraud. The film captures moments that reveal Holmes' deep-seated relationship with untruth.

items.title: 2025 policing trend: Fewer serious crimes, more minor arrests
items.summary: An analysis of 2025 policing trends reveals a decrease in serious crimes but an increase in arrests for minor offenses, such as vagrancy, across the US. This indicates a shift in law enforcement focus even as violent crime rates reach historic lows.

items.title: How Trump's attacks on voting system integrity might affect upcoming elections
items.summary: Election law expert Rick Hasen details how Donald Trump is interfering in upcoming midterm elections by threatening local officials with criminal prosecution if they do not remove alleged noncitizens from voter rolls. These actions raise concerns about the integrity of the voting system.

items.title: Israel detains dozens of Americans, including a congressional candidate, in West Bank
items.summary: Israeli forces detained approximately 80 American and Israeli rabbis and activists, including Democratic congressional candidate Brad Lander, in the West Bank while they were assisting Palestinian olive harvesters. This incident involved a significant number of US citizens.

items.title: New human data hints at psychedelics' potential to combat inflammation
items.summary: New human data suggests that psychedelics, such as psilocybin, may have the potential to reduce inflammation, offering a protective effect for neurodegenerative diseases like Parkinson's. This research builds on previous lab studies showing anti-inflammatory properties.

items.title: Russia releases imprisoned U.S. citizen Stephen Hubbard following Trump's request
items.summary: Russia released imprisoned US citizen Stephen Hubbard at President Trump's request, an announcement made during ongoing talks between Putin and White House envoy Steve Witkoff regarding efforts to end the war in Ukraine. This demonstrates a rare moment of diplomatic success.

items.title: Sentenced to death at 17, at 68, quilt artist receives solo museum exhibition
items.summary: A quilt artist, who was sentenced to death at age 17 and spent decades on death row, is now, at 68, receiving his first solo museum exhibition at the Grand Rapids Art Museum. His journey highlights a remarkable artistic and personal transformation.

items.title: Supreme Court upholds pause on Trump's anti-trans prison policy
items.summary: The Supreme Court ruled to uphold a pause on the Trump administration's anti-transgender prison policy, ensuring that federal prisons must continue providing gender-affirming care to inmates. This decision allows litigation on efforts to change the policy to proceed.

items.title: Trump leans into unprecedented power ahead of midterm elections
items.summary: President Trump is increasingly leveraging unprecedented power ahead of the midterm elections, crossing political barriers he previously avoided in his first term. This behavior signals a more aggressive and less constrained approach to influence the upcoming elections.

items.title: Why local officials are feeling 'on edge' as election day approaches
items.summary: Pennsylvania's chief election official, Al Schmidt, expressed concerns about preparing for the upcoming midterms, recalling how President Trump's insults jeopardized his safety during the 2020 ballot count. Local officials are reportedly feeling "on edge" due to similar pressures.

items.title: Blakeman’s uptown fracking fiesta
items.summary: GOP gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman pledged to halve utility bills by legalizing fracking in New York, though he has not provided detailed policy proposals on how to achieve this or how to cover the resulting financial gap. His claims regarding fracking's impact on costs and the timeline for implementation are questioned.

items.title: The GOP has a midterm messaging problem. Ramaswamy isn’t helping
items.summary: This piece highlights a challenge for the GOP, suggesting the party faces a midterm messaging problem that is not being alleviated by figures like Ramaswamy. It implies internal struggles regarding political communication strategy ahead of elections.

items.title: See Inside Cells Like Never Before in These Vivid Microscopic Images
items.summary: New vivid microscopic images are offering unprecedented views inside cells, enabling researchers to study complex structures like mitochondria in greater detail. This advancement enhances our understanding of cellular organelles and energy generation.

items.title: Battle Drones - a vibe coded RTS with audio-based multiplayer
items.summary: Simon Willison's "Battle Drones" is a browser-based, Command & Conquer-style RTS game developed using AI coding agents, featuring diverse units, maps, and AI personalities. Notably, it supports multiplayer functionality via audio messages or online, improving on earlier game experiments.

items.title: Panache — RTS Belle Époque pour mobile
items.summary: Panache is a delightful French-language fork of the "Battle Drones" RTS game, which has been reskinned to a steampunk 1900s Belle Époque France. This open-source adaptation features new aesthetic updates, including dirigibles and armored automatons, while retaining similar gameplay.

items.title: AI promises productivity, but for managers, it’s mostly a headache for now
items.summary: A new survey indicates that over 50% of managers are experiencing increased difficulty in evaluating employee performance after integrating AI into workflows. This suggests that AI, while promising productivity, currently presents managerial challenges.

items.title: Anthropic pitches AI safety bill that may block a model if 50+ people could be killed
items.summary: Anthropic has proposed an AI safety bill that would restrict federal agencies from blocking an AI model's release unless it could cause over 50 deaths, and only with a judge's approval. Critics suggest this policy may offer weaker protections against AI running amok than it appears.

items.title: Anthropic’s cloud partnerships are getting messy
items.summary: Anthropic is reportedly facing challenges in securing sufficient compute resources from cloud providers, who increasingly view the AI company as a competitor. This situation is contributing to ballooning infrastructure spending ahead of Anthropic's planned November IPO.

items.title: Blacksmith hits unicorn valuation after Sequoia leads Series C
items.summary: Blacksmith, a platform designed for building and testing AI code, has achieved a unicorn valuation of $1 billion after securing a $66 million Series C funding round. The investment was led by Sequoia, highlighting strong confidence in its technology.

items.title: ChatGPT now lets you lock your chats
items.summary: ChatGPT has introduced a new feature allowing users to lock their chats, providing enhanced privacy for personal discussions or planning surprises. This ensures conversations remain confidential when devices are shared.

items.title: Foursquare co-founder says equity holders saw no returns from the company’s acquisition
items.summary: Foursquare's co-founder revealed that the company's equity holders received no returns from its final acquisition, despite the company having raised $411 million in funding. This indicates a significant loss for investors in the location intelligence firm.

items.title: GM is giving OnStar an AI makeover
items.summary: General Motors is implementing one of the most significant overhauls to its 30-year-old OnStar connected car service by integrating advanced AI technology. This "AI makeover" aims to modernize the product and enhance its capabilities.

items.title: GM to close Detroit battery-assembly plant, but not for reasons you might think
items.summary: General Motors is closing its Brownstown Battery Assembly Plant in Detroit, although the company states this decision is not connected to its broader electrification strategy. The plant's closure indicates a shift in its manufacturing operations.

items.title: Google has joined Amazon in attacking Nvidia’s stronghold with AI app developers
items.summary: Google has joined Amazon in releasing developer tools aimed at helping PyTorch users migrate their AI applications away from Nvidia GPUs. This move challenges Nvidia's strong position in the AI app development market by providing alternatives.

items.title: Google is bringing a more personal version of its Gemini AI assistant to your car
items.summary: Google is extending its Gemini AI assistant's Personal Intelligence feature to cars, enabling it to draw upon data from user's Gmail, Calendar, Maps, and YouTube. This integration aims to deliver more personalized and context-aware responses to drivers.

items.title: Heat pump tech is 170 years old — Pascal thinks it’s time for an update
items.summary: Refrigerants startup Pascal is aiming to modernize 170-year-old heat pump technology by introducing a new sponge-like material, which promises to make heat pumps and cooling systems 20% more efficient. This innovation seeks to update outdated thermal transfer methods.

items.title: Hugging Face CEO warns that Netflix’s OpenAI hack documentary isn’t accurate
items.summary: The CEO of Hugging Face, Clem Delangue, warned that the Netflix documentary "AI Gone Rogue," in which he is featured, is inaccurate and takes a "full doomer mode" approach. He advises viewers to be cautious about its portrayal of AI.

items.title: Mach9 raises $34M after pivoting to AI CAD software
items.summary: Mach9 secured $34 million in funding after successfully pivoting its focus from surveying hardware to AI CAD software. The startup's new direction attracted significant investment.

items.title: Meta’s Muse hits 10M US downloads in 40 days, a milestone reached by only 11 other apps
items.summary: Meta's new app, Muse, has achieved 10 million downloads in the US within 40 days, a rapid growth milestone reached by only eleven other applications. Data also indicates that Muse is retaining users at higher rates compared to its AI rivals.

items.title: Waymo starts offering rides at the Las Vegas airport
items.summary: Waymo has expanded its autonomous ride-hailing service to the Las Vegas airport, providing pickups and drop-offs at designated "autonomous vehicle zones" in Terminals 1 and 3. This marks a new operational area for the self-driving car company.

items.title: Are Drug Rehabs Destroying This Small Ohio Town?
items.summary: Portsmouth, Ohio, transformed from an industrial center to a "pill mill HQ" and is now struggling with an overwhelming number of drug recovery centers, some of which reportedly abandon clients at the police station. The city, one of Ohio's poorest, has more recovery beds per capita than any other county.

items.title: Sally Rooney Hates Novels
items.summary: Author Sally Rooney reportedly shows disinterest in promoting her highly successful novels, consistent with her Marxist views on commerce, despite her publisher's extensive marketing campaigns. Her stance highlights a tension between artistic creation and the commercial aspects of the publishing industry.

items.title: Tyler Cowen: Elizabeth Holmes Should Not Be in Prison
items.summary: Economist Tyler Cowen argues that Elizabeth Holmes, convicted of wire fraud for the Theranos scandal, should not be imprisoned because her crimes were non-violent and she has two young children. Instead, he advocates for house arrest and maximum restitution, citing the severe penalty incarceration imposes on her family.

items.title: Corrective for a Broken Heart
items.summary:
“Life will break you,” Louise Erdrich wrote in
her passionate insistence
that “you are here to risk your heart.” It can happen with a shattering, or with a thousand small fissures, but the great paradox — the great salvation — is that every time it happens, you live to see you ar…

items.title: How to Be Un-Dead: Notes on Waking Up from the Trance of Near-Living
items.summary: This article delves into the philosophies of Anaïs Nin and D.H. Lawrence on "livingness," advocating for a process of continuous becoming and resisting the desire to remain in static states. It emphasizes embracing life's full spectrum of experiences, including pain and fulfillment, as central to genuine existence.

items.title: Apple Music has a new logo
items.summary: Apple Music has officially undergone a rebrand, introducing a new logo, an updated wordmark, and a fresh sonic identity crafted by British producer Fred Again and Nest Acoustics. The rebrand visually represents sound influencing visuals, showcasing the logo morphing with water.

items.title: Conversational Gemini navigation comes to Apple CarPlay
items.summary: Google is extending its conversational Gemini AI navigation to Apple CarPlay users in the US, allowing drivers to use voice commands for multi-step questions and hands-free assistance in Google Maps. This feature, already on Android Auto, enables complex queries like finding recommendations and setting routes while avoiding tolls.

items.title: EA is shutting down BioWare
items.summary: Electronic Arts is reportedly shutting down BioWare, the acclaimed studio behind "Mass Effect" and "Dragon Age," and laying off approximately 400 staff. This decision also discontinues development on the next "Mass Effect" game, following EA's recent $55 billion acquisition by an investor group.

items.title: GM promises smarter cars, faster updates, and autonomous dry-cleaning runs
items.summary: General Motors showcased its transformation into a software-defined tech player at its "Onward" event, unveiling initiatives across EV, autonomous vehicles, and AI. GM aims to halve vehicle development times and integrate compute units up to 40 times more powerful than current hardware.

items.title: Supernatural’s comeback starts today, with more music and VR workouts coming soon
items.summary: The popular VR fitness game "Supernatural" has relaunched in early access within the Meta Horizon Store, now independent of Meta. The service offers thousands of remastered and new workouts, with a subscription price increasing from $9.99 to $20 per month or $200 annually.

items.title: They want your blood
items.summary: The "Optimizer" newsletter features a personal account of undergoing frequent blood tests, examining the appeal of longevity apps and health tech that promise to enhance life. The author reflects on the extensive data collection for health optimization.

items.title: Will TP-Link really make routers in the US? Here’s what it told us
items.summary: To overcome a Trump administration ban on foreign-made routers, TP-Link plans to invest nearly $1 billion in US manufacturing, promising hundreds of high-paying jobs. This move aims to allow the company to sell its new Wi-Fi 8 routers in the American market, unlike competitors who received waivers.
